cards.note: Already the official shape: an npm package whose self-contained dsh.bundle patch inserts its own row by bare package name; install verified through `dsh plugin --profile probe add` into dsh.profile.bundles.
Dsh.client (platform web + ./client entry) is declared; no legacy dshClient field and no dsh.plugin.json anywhere in the tree.
The client half declares dsh.client and exports the bundle at ./client, so the client-modules scan accepts the row (boot manifest entry verified live).
Both property-read services (slots, locale) are declared in inject = ['slots','locale']; the only undeclared read was the optional ctx.get('betterLocale') probe, which the A1-10 rebase retires.

The 0.1.1-era optional-service read already used the weak ctx.get form; the rebase removes the probe entirely in favour of the official per-locale register, so no optional service is read by property.
The plugin subscribes to no session/event stream and derives no session state from event fields.
No ctx.sessions or client-runtime session API use: the dock entry is session-scoped by the slot itself, not by session-state aggregation.
No task/run output is tailed; the host half has no runtime work.
The host half injects, calls and listens on no renamed service (httpServer/tasks/onTaskDone).
No ImageAttachmentRef, read_image output or image metadata is consumed or persisted.
The plugin neither registers, wraps, parses nor snapshot-tests read_image.
No custom DeepSeek LLM adapter, image interceptor or attachment cache is involved.
No Host APIProxy call site and no ctx.remote use; the client half talks only to the slots and locale services.
No third-party persisted SessionEvents are produced; the alpha.1 removal is reverted by A2-01 at the final target anyway.
No internal session-view path is imported or patched; all type imports are public /client entries.
No launcher wrapper, SDK/ACP integration or direct profile-file read; the bundle is installed through the official profile path.
No headless wrapper or stdout/stderr parser ships with the plugin.
No tool presentation mode, PTC preset or dispatch-waterfall identifier is used.
The plugin ships no permission, approval, WebFetch policy or audit surface.
No custom loopback HTTP/WS/RPC route or browser page: the client half is served by the official /plugins combo route, so the token/cookie gate is untouched.
Not a model-provider plugin; no provider login configuration is registered.

The third-language override dicts are rebased onto the public locale API (ctx.locale.register(ns, locale, dict), with addLanguage on the language-pack side); the private ctx.get('betterLocale') store probe is retired because better-locale removed that service in its own 0.1.2-alpha.1 adaptation.
No subagent orchestration or provider/model/effort selection is performed.
Informational for the official DeepSeek adapter; the plugin has no adapter code and needs no change.
No persistent PowerShell/Bash or Windows directory-picker workaround is maintained.
No session-log egress path; session-log-deepseek is a deployment choice this plugin does not touch.
The repo ships no browser acceptance script or wrapper; the migration probe itself followed the flow (dsh web --no-open URL, token->cookie 303, __DSH_BOOT__ entry by package name, artifact 200).
No structured-question answerer is registered.
No agent preset is inferred from a persisted session.
No StreamChunk/isTokenDelta processing or TPS computation.
The bundle layer only inserts the plugin's own row; it does not reuse or restate the dsh-base composition, so the telemetry/inventory defaults are untouched.
No direct @earendil-works/pi-ai import; the plugin has no provider or auth code.

dsh-client-runtime is removed from dsh.client.inject, peerDependencies and the JSDoc/type imports; the client context is the Cordis Context and ctx.slots/locale/slot-key declarations come from ui-renderer, dsh-client-locale and ui-conversation.

Assembly row name == package.json name == boot-manifest entry id (checked live on the probe profile); the __ModuleLoader__.load id is stamped by the upstream tsdown build, which this source-only fixture does not ship (see Risks).
No session timeline or user-message content is read; the dock entry receives only framework props.
The composer DOM is never queried or written; the upstream component drives the input machine (inputActions) and renders its own overlay.
No MarkdownText or fenced CodeBlock rendering; the braid label goes through the locale seat.
ctx.connection.api is not used (no history/transcript reads).
No subagent descriptor is constructed or asserted.
No workspace navigation or directory-UI call (connectWorkspace/startSession/pickDirectory/listDirectory/createDirectory).
The plugin persists no SessionEvents, so the restored ignorable retention semantics have no producer here.
No ctx.remote call or RemoteResult handling exists.
No lockfile or install tree exists in this private fixture, so no peer pruning can be proven; every package the type surface references is declared, so no moved-out dependency is missing.
No startup wrapper or CI matrix is maintained here; the probe ran on Node 24.21 (outside the 24.0-24.11.1 failure window).
No pluginInventory/list consumption or PluginInventorySnapshot validation.
ctx.remote.$host.home/isLoopback are not read (no host facts needed).
The plugin bundles no tool/agent package and composes no profile: its dsh.bundle row mounts only itself over dsh-base/dsh-web-app.
No host-side ctx.settings register/update/get call and no test double mirroring that seam.
